name: Roșia Montană Mining Landscape
description: In Romania's Apuseni Mountains, Roșia Montană was the Roman gold-mining town of Alburnus Maior. From 106 CE the Romans dug about 7 km of galleries here, worked waterwheels deep underground, and took out roughly 500 tonnes of gold. Wax-coated writing tablets found in the mines record daily life, and later mine workings and old village farmland still surround the Roman tunnels.
